messages:
jess: Heads up — per-route dashboard shows chat_generate P95 spiking from ~120ms to ~420ms starting around 03:45 UTC, looks correlated with streaming chunk stalls. anyone else see this?

martin: yup I saw the alert. quick glance at the node pool logs suggests the kernel selector flipped to a fallback path on some nodes after 03:42 (memory heuristic kicked in). :thinking:

ryan: throwing up the profiling summary I grabbed:
```
server_emit_ms: 3.2 -> 25.7
chunk_assembly_ms: 0.9 -> 18.4
kv_cache_miss_rate: 4% -> 31%
batch_wait_ms: 1.1 -> 12.6
```
sasha: that kv miss jump is suspicious — was there a change to the kv keying or an index rebuild?

jess: no deploys in that window from apps, but infra-bot shows autoscaler added hosts at ~03:40. could be warmup related.

infra-bot: autoscaler: added 4 instances to runtime-pool-us-west-2 at 03:40:22 due to high CPU usage.

taylor: new instances often boot with baseline kernels until the shim updates; that can increase batch_wait and emit time while kv and kernels warm. martin can you confirm kernel list on the recently added hosts?

martin: checking now — new hosts returned `kernel_shim v2.1` and runtime policy `lowest_mem` which prioritizes smaller-footprint kernels. that explains fallback to lower-perf kernels. I'll prepare a policy tweak to prefer performance kernels for serving pools.

ryan: also worth looking at the batching heuristic: when capacity changes, continuous batching can lengthen batch_hold to fill target batch sizes. suggest lowering `max_batch_hold_ms` for short chat routes like `chat_generate` during the autoscale transient window.

sasha: streaming cadence metrics show lots of 1-token chunks delayed ~15–20ms on the server-side in the regression window. client vs server breakdown I pulled: 
- client_send_ms: ~2ms
- network: ~6ms
- server_emit_ms: ~18ms (was ~3ms baseline)
So majority is server-side emission.

jess: action list: (1) martin: revert the selection policy bump and force the perf kernel on the new hosts, (2) taylor: roll a canary with a stricter `max_batch_hold_ms` for `chat_generate`, (3) ryan: run kv-cache warmup/flush on the 4 hosts and monitor miss rate, (4) infra-bot: alert the channel when new instances join.

martin: on it — will revert policy and push `kernel_shim v2.3` to the pool, then pin selection policy to `prefer_perf` for serving nodes. will update when done.

taylor: starting canary for reduced batch hold now, will report P95 in ~5m. :thumbsup:

deploy-bot: canary for `chat_generate-batching-rollout` started at 03:57:10 UTC (instance subset: runtime-pool-us-west-2/hosts-045).

ryan: ran the warmup script against the 4 new hosts — kv miss rate dropped from ~31% to ~7% after ~2 minutes of synthetic warms.

sasha: canary metrics look promising so far — P95 down to ~130ms, server_emit_ms back toward baseline. watching for recurring stalls.

jess: great work — if canary holds for 10m we promote. please post any additional anomalies here. thanks all :rocket:
